/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs && python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('Pages:',len(r.pages))
print('Metadata:',r.metadata)
parts=[]
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages):
 t=p.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
 parts.append(f'\\n\\n===== PAGE {i+1} =====\\n'+t)
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text(''.join(parts))
print(''.join(parts)[:29000])
PY"

strengths: AiT presents a coherent architectural combination of persistent low-dimensional memory, competition among patches across a batch, and associative retrieval. Using the same memory to guide selection and reconstruct representations is a potentially useful contribution.

Table 1 shows meaningful improvements over comparable ViT configurations. AiT-Small achieves 83.34%/56.30% on CIFAR-10/100 versus 79.53%/53.19% for ViT-Small, with 15.8M versus 14.9M parameters. AiT-Medium also exceeds ViT-Base on both datasets while using substantially fewer parameters.

The component ablations provide useful supporting evidence. Removing the bottleneck reduces CIFAR-10 accuracy from 83.34% to 75.40%, while replacing Hopfield retrieval with multi-head attention reduces it to 81.03% (Table 2). Initialization and temperature experiments further characterize the design.

Evaluation extends to relational reasoning, where AiT improves over Coordination from 73.43% to 76.82% (Table 4). The fixed-memory inference ablation is also informative: disabling memory forwarding changes CIFAR-100 accuracy only from 60.58% to 60.56% (Table 7), supporting the usefulness of the stored memory.
weaknesses: The proposed balance loss has a consequential specification and optimization problem. Equation 5 uses attention scores previously defined by dense softmax, making every positivity indicator one and the load variance zero. If post-top-k scores are intended, the hard counts still have zero gradient almost everywhere, with no surrogate described. Figures 9–10 show changes during training without a loss-disabled control, so they do not establish that this novel loss causes specialization or improves accuracy.

The Hopfield contribution is overstated and its implementation incompletely specified. The standard update associated with Equation 7 is a softmax-weighted memory read with tied keys and values, undermining the claimed fundamental distinction from attention. Equation 8 specifies an argmin, whereas the text reports one unspecified update; energy reduction does not establish exact minimization or convergence to an individual stored prior. Replacing retrieval with a fully parameterized multi-head attention module does not isolate the claimed conceptual advantage.

The computational claims are not adequately supported. Forming the M-by-(BN) attention scores still scales with input quantity before top-k selection, projections depend on input dimension, and AiT retains ordinary quadratic self-attention. The complexity statement in Section 4.1 therefore does not characterize the complete architecture or demonstrate input-invariant computation. Parameter counts alone cannot establish runtime or memory savings, and no FLOPs, latency, or peak-memory measurements are supplied.

Important attribution and inference questions remain unresolved. There is no training ablation disabling only cross-sample squashing, and the relational reasoning comparison lacks a ViT baseline despite AiT adding self-attention relative to Coordination. Standard inference also depends on the current test batch through temporary memory computation. Appendix A.5 provides a useful alternative, but batch-size and batch-composition sensitivity are not evaluated.

Reproducibility and reporting need clarification. Section 5.1 gives a learning rate of 1e-5, whereas Table 6 gives 1e-4; gradient handling through memory across batches is unspecified, and the main tables omit variability despite averaging three runs. Figure 7 also interprets raw counts inconsistently: 47–49 patches out of 65 exceed 50%, contrary to the description of many highlighted heads. These reporting issues are secondary to the central concerns about the learning mechanism and computational claims, which determine the Weak Reject recommendation.
